causes.label: Automatic renewal fails silently: the DNS API token of the ACME account was rotated and the renewal jobs were not re-tested
causes.check: Look at the last run of the renewal job and at the age of the DNS API token of the shared ACME account.

causes.label: The certificate was installed by hand and is not in the renewal inventory
causes.check: Check whether the certificate is listed in the renewal inventory.

causes.label: Debug logging stayed on after a release and fills the volume
causes.check: Check the size of the log directory and the logging level since the last release.

causes.label: The archive share has no retention rule and grows until the disk is full
causes.check: Check the growth per week of the archive share and whether a retention rule exists.

causes.label: A firewall clean-up closed the outgoing path to the supplier endpoint
causes.check: Test the connection from the integration host to the supplier endpoint.

causes.label: The supplier replaced its intermediate certificate and the trust store of the host is outdated
causes.check: Compare the certificate chain the supplier sends with the trust store of the host.

cases.title: Edge certificate nearly expired, renewal did not run

findings.text: The renewal job reported no error but had not renewed the certificate for 40 days.
The DNS API token of the ACME account had been rotated two weeks before.
The certificate expired because the renewal job failed to answer the DNS challenge.
Manual renewal was blocked by the change freeze and needed an emergency approval.

cases.title: Renewal job without effect at Alpenwerk

findings.text: The job ran every night and wrote success, but the challenge record was never created.
A new DNS API token solved it; the old one had no write right any more.
The certificate had been installed by hand in 2025 and was not in the renewal inventory.
Debug logging had been switched on for a test and stayed on after the release.
The log directory grew by 6 GB a day.
The archive share grows by about 2 GB a week and has no retention rule.
The volume was extended; the problem came back within five months.
Old validation records were never deleted because no retention rule existed.
A retention rule of 18 months solved it for good.

cases.title: Supplier sync timeouts after a firewall change

findings.text: The nightly sync timed out because a firewall clean-up had removed the outgoing rule to the supplier.
Reopening the rule fixed the sync at once.

cases.title: Supplier sync fails with a certificate error

findings.text: The supplier had replaced its intermediate certificate and the host did not trust the new chain.
The sync showed timeouts, not a certificate error, because the library retried silently.
Before the run, check that the DNS API token of the ACME account is valid and has the right to write the challenge record.

docs.title: Post-mortem: silent renewal failures after the February secret rotation

findings.text: After the secret rotation on 2026-02-12 the renewal jobs of three customers ran without an error code but did not renew.
Follow-up: re-test every renewal job after each secret rotation.
2026-07-30: DNS API token of the shared ACME account rotated; the renewal jobs were not re-tested afterwards.
Archive volumes of customers with a premium contract grow by 1 to 3 GB a week; a retention rule is defined only for new contracts.
Volumes above 90 percent are extended on request; this treats the symptom only.
2026-10-14: clean-up of unused egress rules; three rules for supplier address ranges were removed, one of them for the procurement platform.
